note: Human review of the derived ligament attachments, applied by src/scripts/generateLigamentSeed.ts. Derivation measures which bones a ligament mesh TOUCHES; this file records where touching is not attaching, and where a human has confirmed that it is. An entry with `confirmed: true` and no `attachmentStructureIds` keeps the derived set and only clears needsReview. Regenerating the seed re-applies this file, so a correction is never lost to a re-run. Entries sourced to the review page are the user's own ticks, read back from the artifact database.

deep-transverse-metatarsal-ligament.description: A series of short transverse bands joining the plantar plates of adjacent metatarsophalangeal joints, binding the heads of the metatarsals together and holding the forefoot as a unit.
deep-transverse-metatarsal-ligament.source: Labelled dorsal foot diagram and Netter plantar/lateral foot plate, supplied 13 Sept 2026
deep-transverse-metatarsal-ligament.why: It runs head to head between the plantar plates and never reaches a phalanx. The derived contact with the proximal phalanges is the mesh lying against their bases — the clearest case in the tranche of touching not being attaching.

deep-transverse-metacarpal-ligament.description: Short transverse bands joining the palmar plates of the second to fifth metacarpophalangeal joints, binding the metacarpal heads together. The thumb is free of it, which is part of why it opposes.
deep-transverse-metacarpal-ligament.source: By the same anatomy as the foot band above, which the supplied plates settle; standard teaching for the hand
deep-transverse-metacarpal-ligament.why: The hand's band is the metatarsal band's counterpart and attaches the same way — plate to plate across the metacarpal heads, not to the phalanges. Derivation put the metacarpals top anyway (3rd 22%, 2nd 17%, 4th 17%).

plantar-metatarsophalangeal-ligaments.source: Netter lateral inset, 'Capsule and ligaments of metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints'
plantar-metatarsophalangeal-ligaments.why: The plantar plate runs from the plantar aspect of the metatarsal head to the base of the proximal phalanx, which is what the derived pair already says.

collateral-metacarpophalangeal-ligaments.source: Same lateral inset, and the collateral ligaments labelled at the MTP joints of the dorsal diagram
collateral-metacarpophalangeal-ligaments.why: A collateral runs from the tubercle on the metacarpal head to the base of the proximal phalanx. Derived pair is right.

palmar-interphalangeal-ligaments.source: Netter lateral inset, which draws the plate at the interphalangeal joint between middle and distal phalanx
palmar-interphalangeal-ligaments.why: These are the palmar plates of the PIP and DIP joints together, so all three phalangeal rows are genuinely involved: proximal and middle at the PIP, middle and distal at the DIP.

ulnar-collateral-ligament.why: CONFIRMED BY THE USER AS DERIVED, but flagged: the elbow UCL runs medial epicondyle to coronoid process and olecranon, and standard teaching gives it no radial attachment. The radius contact is probably the mesh lying against the radial head. Raise before deploy.

ulnocapitate-ligament.source: User review on the review page, 13 Sept 2026
ulnocapitate-ligament.why: CONFIRMED BY THE USER AS DERIVED, but flagged: the ulnocapitate runs from the ulna (fovea / palmar radioulnar ligament) to the capitate and passes over the lunate rather than attaching to it, so the 25% lunate contact is probably passage. The supplied wrist plate does not label it, so this rests on standard teaching. Raise before deploy.

ulnolunate-ligament.description: A palmar ulnocarpal ligament running from the ulna, by way of the palmar radioulnar ligament and the triangular fibrocartilage, to the lunate.
ulnolunate-ligament.source: Labelled palmar wrist plate supplied 13 Sept 2026 (ulnolunate drawn from the ulnar head region to the lunate)
ulnolunate-ligament.why: It arises with the palmar radioulnar ligament and inserts on the lunate. The derived scaphoid and capitate contact is the strap lying against the carpus on its way; only the lunate is an attachment.
